cvEn:
Hanoh Shwartz, son of Miriam and Zelig, was born on 23 Cheshvan 5691 (14 November 1930) in the city of Lodz, Poland. In 1933, when he was two years old, his parents immigrated to the Land of Israel. Hanoh completed his elementary schooling in Holon.

On the day of his Bar Mitzvah, he read aloud before his parents and many guests: "On the day of my passage, I make the accounting of my world, as a son of my people, as a son of the Hebrew nation - - - I will stand in line together with my friends; I will gird strength so that we may remove from ourselves and from all our people the chains of exile, and wipe away the disgrace of our people."

When the War of Independence broke out, following the United Nations General Assembly's decision to partition the country into two states, he enlisted and served in the Kiryati Brigade as a squad commander in Holon. Hanoh fell on 6 Iyar 5708 (15 May 1948) during the bombing of the Dov airfield in Tel Aviv. He was laid to rest in the military cemetery at Nahalat Yitzhak.
